summary_en: Ihara announced an update on capital cost-conscious management. The company targets PBR above 1.0x through revenue growth, shareholder returns at 35-40% payout ratio and 50% total return ratio during the 6th Medium-Term Plan (2025-2027), and enhanced IR/SR activities. Operating profit rose 20.1% year-on-year in Q3 FY2026.
title_en: Response to Realize Management Conscious of Cost of Capital and Stock Price (Update)
translation_en_brief:
Ihara announced an update on its capital cost-conscious management strategy at a board meeting on November 16, 2026. The company acknowledges that while sales, operating profit, ROIC and ROE have remained stable and PBR has improved from previous periods, the target of sustaining PBR above 1.0x remains unachieved. Management attributes this partly to investor concerns about the concrete measures for medium- to long-term revenue expansion through growth investment, despite growing understanding of shareholder return policy and growth strategy.

To realize PBR exceeding 1.0x, the company commits to three pillars: (1) enhancing profitability through sales expansion, technology development, productivity improvements using robotics and AI, and DX initiatives; (2) maintaining and improving shareholder returns through a dividend payout ratio of 35-40% and total return ratio of 50% during the 6th Medium-Term Plan (2025-2027); and (3) strengthening IR and SR activities. For FY2025 (ended December 2025), the company paid 118 yen per share dividend (payout ratio 35.4%), up 18 yen from 100 yen in FY2024. FY2026 dividend guidance is 118 yen per share at approximately 35% payout ratio.

Operating performance showed Q3 FY2026 results of 5.1% sales growth and 20.1% operating profit growth year-over-year compared to Q3 FY2025. The company will pursue revenue expansion and profit margin improvement under the 6th Medium-Term Plan while simultaneously investing in and expanding into growth sectors including disaster prevention, national resilience, infrastructure DX, renewable energy, decarbonization, and marine robotics, including M&A opportunities.
